title: Sir James Somerville is Lord Mayor of Dublin
desc: James Somerville, MP for Dublin City since 1729, serves as Lord Mayor {s:wp-sir-james-somerville}.

title: Somerville baronetcy created
desc: James Somerville is created a baronet "of Somerville, Co. Meath"; he dies that August and is succeeded by his eldest son Quaile {s:wp-sir-james-somerville}. The narrator's "first baronet" {q:84}.

title: Major William Somerville inherits Ardrass
desc: The second son of the first baronet "inherited an estate in County Kildare called Ardrass … a large house and a lot of land", let to tenants as was usual {q:84-86}. The NLI pedigree of the Somervilles of Ardrass begins in 1752 {s:nli-ardrass}.

title: Henry Bellingham marries Elizabeth Tenison
desc: Eliza Bellingham's parents marry in Dublin {s:lf-bellingham}. The Tenison name will reappear in two generations.

title: Captain William Somerville born
desc: The narrator: "he was born in 1777, I think" {q:62}; the published Bellingham genealogy gives 1776 {s:lf-bellingham}.

title: Eliza Bellingham born
desc: Published date {s:lf-bellingham}.

title: Alan Bellingham marries Monique Bâby at Detroit
desc: Eliza's brother Alan, who had gone to Canada as a young man, marries the French-Canadian Monique Bâby {q:30} {s:lf-bellingham}.

title: William Bellingham, Pitt's secretary, made a baronet
desc: Created baronet "of Castle Bellingham" with remainder to his father's heirs {s:wp-bellingham-bt}.

title: Rebellion of 1798
desc: The United Irishmen's rising. The North Cork Militia, one of the regiments Captain William may have served in {q:54-56}, became notorious for its conduct in the rebellion in Wexford {s:wp-irish-militia}.

title: Captain William Somerville marries Eliza Bellingham
desc: "He married Eliza Bellingham, I think 1800" {q:60-62}; the published genealogy gives Roscrea, 30 August 1800 {s:lf-bellingham}. Half his interest in Ardrass goes into the marriage settlement {q:88-90}.

title: Lt-Col. Henry Bellingham dies; Alan inherits Castle Bellingham
desc: Published account {s:lf-bellingham}.

title: Archibald James Somerville born
desc: "He was born in 1803, is it? Yes" {q:128}.

title: Henry Tenison Bellingham killed at Badajoz
desc: Eliza's younger brother, a captain, is killed in the storming of Badajoz {q:44, 52} {s:lf-bellingham}. Years later Eliza writes on the anniversary that her brother "was killed on this day, so many years ago".

title: Siege of Badajoz
desc: Wellington's Anglo-Portuguese army besieges and storms the French-held fortress; the assault costs thousands of allied casualties {s:wp-badajoz}. (Waterloo, which the narrator wondered about, was in 1815; the "War of 1812" was a separate Anglo-American conflict.)

title: Alan and Monique Bellingham separate
desc: "Their marriage was not successful" {q:40}. Monique settles at Lyme Regis, Alan in London {s:lf-bellingham}.

title: Castle Bellingham passes to Sir William Bellingham
desc: Narrator: Alan "sold it, actually, to his uncle" {q:36-38}. Published account: Alan had rented the estate to Sir William, and his widow sold the freehold by about 1824 {s:lf-bellingham}.

title: Archibald James leaves home for Barbados
desc: While Eliza and Dorothea are in Dublin, Archibald, about 19, leaves home, "spent a few days [in Clonmel?] and then took ship on board the George and Thomas for the Barbados". He had "got a girl into the family way" {q:16-18, 142-150}.

title: Birth of "little Archie"
desc: Letters arrive from Madeira and Barbados; one names the child Archibald. Captain William and Eliza take responsibility for "little Archie", paying a succession of wet nurses {q:154-162}.

title: Sir William Bellingham dies
desc: Succeeded by his nephew Sir Alan, 2nd Bt, whose line held Castle Bellingham until c. 1956 {s:wp-bellingham-bt}.

title: The family moves from Cumry to "Farm", then to Dublin
desc: From Cumry to a house "just called Farm" (probably near Belturbet, Co. Cavan) for a few years, then to Bayview Avenue/Crescent, Dublin {q:182-184}. Dates not given.

title: Irish Constabulary formed
desc: The Irish Constabulary Act amalgamates the provincial forces into a single armed, centrally controlled Irish Constabulary {s:wp-ric}.

title: Eliza Somerville (née Bellingham) dies
desc: "Eliza died, 1839" {q:186}; "the family then went into decline" {q:198}. Day from the published genealogy {s:lf-bellingham}.

title: Tenison Alan returns from Trinidad
desc: After his mother's death he "returned to Ireland in 1840 … and secured an appointment", and married Eliza O'Connor {q:204-208}.

title: Deaths of Bellingham and of Captain William Somerville
desc: Father and son had moved to lodgings north of the Liffey. "Bellingham died in the autumn of 1844, and Captain William died in December 1844" {q:198-200}.

title: The Great Famine
desc: Potato blight brings famine, mass death and emigration. The narrator does not mention it, but it frames the years in which Tenison Alan built his career at Dublin Castle and his cousin Sir William served as Chief Secretary {s:wp-great-famine} {s:wp-1st-baron}.

title: Sir William Somerville is Chief Secretary for Ireland
desc: Tenison's "cousin" holds the office responsible for Irish administration and police {s:wp-1st-baron}; the narrator credits him with Tenison's Constabulary appointment {q:212-214}.

title: Bellingham Arthur Somerville born
desc: "He was born in '56 … I think it was 1856" {q:2}.

title: Monique Bellingham dies at Lyme Regis
desc: Published account {s:lf-bellingham}.

title: The Constabulary becomes "Royal"
desc: After the Fenian Rising of 1867 the Irish Constabulary is granted the prefix "Royal" {s:wp-ric}.

title: Archibald James Somerville dies (?)
desc: "He died in 1871, I think" {q:128}. Unverified.

title: W. A. T. B. ("Bunt") Somerville born
The Plan of Campaign
desc: Tenants on selected estates withhold rent collectively during the agricultural depression; the Ponsonby estate near Youghal is among the first targeted {s:wp-plan-of-campaign} {s:ballymacoda-1887}.

title: The Youghal riot: Patrick Hanlon killed
desc: Family account: a riot at Youghal "got out of hand"; RIC sent by train from Cork "under the command of Captain Somerville"; a rioter "Hanlon or O'Hann" killed with a blade; Somerville and the man responsible held and suspended; the matter raised in Parliament; Somerville acquitted and reinstated {q:312-322}. Published accounts: during protests over the arrest of Fr Daniel Keller, the RIC charged with fixed bayonets and Patrick Hanlon, a 30-year-old fisherman from Ballymacoda, was killed by a sword bayonet. The coroner's jury found wilful murder against District Inspector Somerville and Constable Garrett Ward, both taken to Cork gaol; questions were asked in the Commons (18 and 24 March 1887); the Crown entered a nolle prosequi {s:ballymacoda-1887} {s:hansard-1887}. The narrator asked that this story be handled with discretion {q:290}.

title: Bellingham Arthur transferred to Wicklow
desc: With his health poor and his future in the RIC "questionable", he applies for a transfer to Wicklow, where he is District Inspector {q:324-328}.

title: Bellingham Arthur acquires Clermont
desc: Colonel Tottenham buys Clermont at auction and sells it on at cost to Bellingham Arthur, the underbidder {q:574-580}. The house's wings are added in 1894 for "B A Somerville" to designs by Sir Thomas Drew {s:wicklowheritage-clermont}.

title: Eliza O'Connor (Mrs Tenison Somerville) dies
desc: Tenison had died first {q:216}. Around this time young Eddie destroys parts of Captain William's diary {q:134}.

title: Reginald Somerville born at Clermont
desc: The youngest child and the only one born at Clermont; he was 17 when war broke out in 1914 {q:348, 574}.

title: Cecilia Somerville marries Henry Rock
desc: "She's finally married in 1912" {q:246}.

title: Pat captured in the retreat from Mons
desc: {q:440-442} The BEF fought at Mons on 23 August 1914 and then fell back for two weeks towards the Marne {s:wp-mons} {s:wp-great-retreat}.

title: Pat's third escape succeeds
desc: After two recaptures he crosses Germany and Holland to London, is disbelieved at the War Office, and receives the Military Cross {q:446-450}. Date not given.

title: Bellingham Arthur Somerville dies
desc: Of "the flu that was then going around"; the narrator rightly doubts it was the Spanish flu {q:2, 10-12}.

title: Reginald at Passchendaele
desc: A second lieutenant in the Royal Warwickshire Regiment {q:356-358}. The Third Battle of Ypres ran from July to November 1917 {s:wp-passchendaele}.

title: The influenza pandemic reaches Ireland
desc: Three waves (June 1918, October 1918, February 1919) kill over 20,000 people in Ireland {s:dcc-flu}. Bellingham Arthur's death in 1916 predates it {q:10-12}.

title: Bunt commands troops at Archangel
desc: "He commanded a troop that was sent to Archangel … to keep it from falling into the hands of the Bolsheviks" {q:364}. Lt-Col W.A.T.B. Somerville DSO took command of the 8th (Special) Battalion, Machine Gun Corps on 12 April 1919; it landed at Archangel on 26 May {s:mgc-8bn} {s:wp-north-russia}.

title: Reginald goes to Kenya
desc: With "Gunners Venture", to manage coffee near Nanyuki; he travels up with an ox cart {q:496-504}.

title: The Burning of Cork
desc: Crown forces burn much of Cork city centre during the War of Independence {s:wp-burning-cork}. Raised by the interviewer, not by the family's story {q:602-606}.

title: Public Record Office destroyed in the Four Courts
desc: At the start of the Civil War an explosion and fire destroy the Public Record Office of Ireland and centuries of records, including most 19th-century census returns {s:irishtimes-pro} {s:tcd-beyond2022}. Bellingham Arthur's notes, made before 1916, preserve information from records now lost {q:4}.

title: Somerville baronetcy becomes dormant
desc: The 2nd Baron Athlumney dies without issue; his peerages become extinct and the baronetcy dormant {q:174} {s:wp-2nd-baron}.

title: Maud dies on the voyage home
desc: Two years after Juanita's birth, travelling home to show her to the family; Reginald "arrived back in Ireland a widower" {q:508-510}.

title: Reginald marries Honor Johnson
desc: Childhood friends who met again at Clermont {q:512-514}.

title: Margaret Somerville (née Clinch) dies
desc: Clermont is left empty; Reginald looks after it. Her domicile is disputed between the Irish and English Revenue {q:380, 386, 548}.

title: Uncle Jim dies after a last year at Clermont
Uncle Bunt dies months after deciding to live at Clermont
Dispute and sale of Clermont
desc: Aunt Eddie threatens action against Bunt's widow over his administration of their mother's estate; after "peace talks" half the proceeds go to the rest of the family. The house sells for £10,000 {q:558-566}. A heritage record dates the sale c. 1955 {s:wicklowheritage-clermont}.

title: Ardrass house demolished
desc: "The main house was pulled down in the 1950s" after a large sale of contents {q:94}.

title: Clermont becomes a convent school
desc: The Religious of Christian Education, invited by Archbishop McQuaid, open a school at Clermont; it closes around 2004–05, and the site later becomes a college campus {s:irishaesthete-clermont} {s:wp-rathnew}.

title: Ballynatray sold, reportedly to Sir James Dyson
desc: "Which now belongs to Mr. Dyson" {q:312}. Widely reported but not officially confirmed {s:agriland-ballynatray}.

title: The conversation is recorded
desc: The transcript file is dated 27 October; the narrator is "coming up to 90" (born 1937) and it is half-term {q:50, 310}, which points to 2026, though the year is not stated. See {qn:q-recording-date}.
